# COR060 `unchecked-stat`

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="enabled by default" />

The `stat=` variable of an `allocate`/`deallocate` is never read afterwards.

## Why

Passing `stat=` tells the runtime not to stop on failure: the error is reported only through the
variable. If nothing reads it, an allocation failure is silently ignored and the program continues
with an unallocated array.

## Reported

```fortran
allocate(a(n), stat=ierr)
a = 0.0
```

## Preferred

```fortran
allocate(a(n), stat=ierr)
if (ierr /= 0) error stop 'cannot allocate a'
```

## Suppressing

For one occurrence, with the reason on the same line (or alone on the line before the statement):

```fortran
! fobis: ignore[COR060] <why this occurrence is fine>
```

For the whole project, `ignore = COR060` in the fobos [`[lint]` section](/cookbook/analysis#choose-the-rules).

## Equivalent

Fortitude rule `C181` (see [Lint Rules](/lint-rules/#relation-to-fortitude)).
